To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a distributed neural network implementation of a production rule interpreter can perform pattern matching and variable bindings; (2) the network can learn new rules; (3) the network can be trained using supervised learning; (4) the network can perform inductive generalization; (5) the network can use a variety of knowledge representation formalisms; (6) the network can reason with incomplete information; (7) the network can handle noisy data.

pattern matching and variable-binding operations are implemented in a neural network by a combination of lateral inhibition and a form of Hebbian learning, and that the resulting architecture is a production system interpreter.
pattern matching and variable-binding are emergent properties of a connectionist production system interpreter.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of what is the minimum set of mechanisms required to perform symbolic reasoning, and whether these mechanisms can emerge from the collective activity of a network of simple neuron-like elements.
the following questions: How can the operations of pattern matching and variable substitution be implemented in connectionist systems?
the implementation of a production interpreter in an artificial neural network using distributed symbolic representations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the connectionist approach can be used to implement symbolic inference.
we have demonstrated that a connectionist architecture can perform a variety of symbolic reasoning tasks and that the performance is competitive with conventional symbolic approaches.
connectionists have a long way to go to prove that their theories are as powerful as symbolic theories, but that they are not as far from that goal as they might have been thought.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the connectionist approach to symbol processing can be made to work.
we show how the connectionist approach can implement a symbolic reasoning architecture, and how this can be achieved with minimal additional machinery.
we have demonstrated that connectionist systems have the potential to do symbolic reasoning and that they can do so in a way that is very similar to how we believe humans do symbolic reasoning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
connectionist systems are not only able to perform symbolic inference, but that they can do so with a degree of efficiency and flexibility that is difficult for conventional architectures to match.
a distributed representation of rules and symbols is a natural way for a neural network to perform symbolic inference.

a connectionist production system is capable of performing symbolic reasoning, but the implementation is different from the conventional symbolic implementation in that it is a massively parallel, distributed system.
